strategy.summary: Reproduce sklearn issue #32178 / PR #32351: DecisionTreeRegressor with NaN-containing X and feature-order-dependent partitioning yields wrong impurity ([0.25,0.1875,0.1875] instead of [0.25,0,0]) on the buggy commit b1b01a1611e1; the developer test test_splitting_with_missing_values in sklearn/tree/tests/test_tree.py must fail there and pass after the fix. Build scikit-learn from source at the buggy commit (Cython extensions in sklearn/tree need compiling), apply the developer test, and run it.

build_commands: pip install -r requirements or pip install numpy==2.3.3 scipy==1.16.2 Cython==3.1.3 joblib threadpoolctl pytest meson-python ninja
pinned_because: numpy 2.3.3 and scipy 1.16.2 are the versions in the issue #32178 reproducer environment; documented=false, so they are chosen from the evidence, not from a documented constraint
Cython 3.1.3 is the reproducer's version; no documented constraint, chosen for build reproducibility
joblib and threadpoolctl have only placeholder README minimums (|JoblibMinVersion|, |ThreadpoolctlMinVersion|); they are not numerically relevant so latest compatible versions are used

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy b1b01a1611e1 the test fails: for some i in range(20) the fitted tree's impurity is [0.25, 0.1875, 0.1875] rather than [0.25, 0., 0.], so assert_array_equal raises AssertionError. On the fixed revision (with PR #32351 applied) all 20 fits give impurity [0.25, 0., 0.] and the test passes. The transition fail-to-pass is the whole criterion.

input_output_examples.input: X = np.vstack([[0,0,0,0,1,2,3,4],[1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2]]).swapaxes(0,1).astype(float); y=[0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1]; X[X==0]=np.nan; DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=1, random_state=i).fit(X, y) for i in range(20)
input_output_examples.expected_output: tree.tree_.impurity == [0.25 0. 0.] for every i in range(20)

input_output_examples.input: same X and y with NaN, DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=1, random_state=i, min_impurity_decrease=0.002).fit(X, y) for broken random state i=2

risks: The bug is random-state dependent (feature-order dependent); the developer test iterates range(20) to cover both feature orders, so the failure should appear, but it is not guaranteed for every build. Failure is probabilistic (~50% of fits per issue) and not a deterministic single-fit reproduction.

The versions numpy 2.3.3, scipy 1.16.2, Cython 3.1.3 come from the issue reporter's environment, not a documented constraint; era_ceiling is null, so compatibility with the buggy commit is assumed rather than verified. If the build fails with these pins, relax to the nearest compatible versions.

Numerical backend is OpenBLAS (libscipy_openblas, Haswell architecture) with OpenMP via libgomp; the tree splitter itself does not depend on BLAS, but the reporter's platform was x86_64 Haswell. The defect is not documented as platform-specific, so it is expected to appear on other x86_64 Linux builds, but this is not established by the evidence.
Building scikit-learn from source requires a C/C++ compiler and OpenMP; a build without OpenMP may change threading but not the tree-splitting logic.
Reproducer relies on X[X==0]=np.nan which changes feature ordering; results depend on the sklearn version before the fix, so the test must be run against the exact buggy commit, not a later mainline.
The exact fraction of broken trees (~50%) is approximate and may vary across runs; the test is designed to hit both feature orders with 20 random states.
python_version is null (not stated by evidence); any Python version supported by numpy 2.3.3 and scipy 1.16.2 should work, but this is not verified.

oracle.reference_source: developer test assert_array_equal against np.array([0.25, 0.0, 0.0]) in PR #32351
oracle.why: The test compares impurity arrays exactly; the expected values are exact fractions of the fixed split, so exact comparison is the project's own oracle.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision, for some random_state in range(20) the off-by-one in partitioning with missing values yields impurity [0.25, 0.1875, 0.1875] instead of [0.25, 0., 0.]; assert_array_equal raises AssertionError, so the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With PR #32351 applied, every random_state in range(20) yields impurity [0.25, 0., 0.], so assert_array_equal succeeds and the test passes.
